'''Craig Dworkin''' is an American poet, critic, editor, and Professor of English at the [[University of Utah]].<ref name="Faculty Page">{{cite web |title=Craig Dworkin |url=https://faculty.utah.edu/u0455611-CRAIG_DWORKIN/research/index.hml |website=The University of Utah |access-date=1 July 2021}}</ref><ref name="Warhol Arts Writers Grant">{{cite web |title=Craig Dworkin |url=https://www.artswriters.org/grant/grantees/grantee/craig_dworkin |website=The Andy Warhol Foundation Arts Writers Grant |access-date=24 December 2022 |date=2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Craig Dworkin |url=https://mappingliteraryutah.org/utah-writers/craig-dworkin |website=Mapping Literary Utah |access-date=24 December 2022}}</ref> He is the founding senior editor of Eclipse, an online archive of 20th-century small-press writing and 21st-century born-digital publications.<ref name="Jacket2 Eclipse Interview">{{cite web |last1=LaMarre |first1=James |title=Poetic protocols: An interview with Craig Dworkin |url=http://jacket2.org/interviews/poetic-protocols |website=Jacket2 |access-date=1 July 2021 |date=5 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gossett |first1=Michael |title=Eclipse Archive |url=https://archivalencounters.commons.gc.cuny.edu/eclipse-archive/ |website=Archival Encounters |access-date=24 December 2022 |date=4 March 2019}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Dworkin received his BA from [[Stanford University]] and his PhD from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="Warhol Arts Writers Grant" /> He was an [[Assistant professor|assistant]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Assistant professors join faculty |url=https://pr.princeton.edu/pwb/98/1116/join.htm |website=Princeton Weekly Bulletin |access-date=1 July 2021 |date=16 November 1998}}</ref> and [[associate professor]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Board approves 14 promotions |url=https://pr.princeton.edu/pwb/04/0419/2b.shtml |website=Princeton Weekly Bulletin |access-date=1 July 2021 |date=2004}}</ref> at [[Princeton University]] from 1998 to 2004 before joining the faculty at the [[University of Utah]], where he is a Professor of English.<ref name="Faculty Page" />

Dworkin has written a number of books of poetry, including ''Helicography'' (Punctum Books, 2021),<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sacksteder |first1=Joe |title="Helicography by Craig Dworkin" |url=https://www.therupturemag.com/rupture/helicography |website=The Rupture |access-date=24 December 2022 |date=April 2022}}</ref> ''The Pine-Woods Notebook'' (Kenning Editions, 2019),<ref>{{cite web |title=Al Filreis and Danny Snelson discuss The Pine-Woods Notebook |url=https://www.kenningeditions.com/kenning-editions/al-filreis-and-danny-snelson-discuss-the-pine-woods-notebook/ |website=Kenning Dworkin is the author of four scholarly monographs: ''Radium of the Word: A Poetics of Materiality'' ([[University of Chicago Press|Chicago]], 2020);<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Virginia |title=Virginia Jackson reviews Radium of the Word |url=https://criticalinquiry.uchicago.edu/virginia_jackson_reviews_radium_of_the_word/ |website=Critical Inquiry |access-date=24 December 2022 |url=https://lareviewofbooks.org/article/the-poet-and-the-dictionary/ |website=The Los Angeles Review of Books |access-date=1 July 2021 |date=7 November 2020}}</ref> ''No Medium'' ([[MIT Press|MIT]], |website=The Los Angeles Review of Books |access-date=1 July 2021 |date=9 July 2013}}</ref> in which he discusses works that are "blank, erased, clear, or silent";<ref>{{cite web |last1=Leong |first1=Michael |title=Reading the "Nothings that Are": Craig Dworkin's "No Medium" |url=https://hyperallergic.com/72790/reading-the-nothings-that-are-craig-dworkins-no-medium/ |website=Hyperallergic Consequence of Innovation: 21st Century Poetics'' (Roof, 2008). He has published articles in such diverse journals as ''October'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig Douglas |title=Fugitive Signs |journal=October |date=Winter 2001 |volume=95 |pages=90–113 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/779201 |access-date=24 December 2022 |publisher=The MIT Press|jstor=779201 }}</ref> ''[[Grey Room]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig |title=Whereof One Cannot Speak |journal=Grey Room |date=Fall 2005 |volume=21 |issue=21 |pages=46–69 |doi=10.1162/152638105774539798 |url=https://direct.mit.edu/grey/article/doi/10.1162/152638105774539798/10461/Whereof-One-Cannot-Speak |access-date=1 July 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref> ''[[Contemporary Literature (journal)|Contemporary Literature]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig |title=The Imaginary Solution |journal=Contemporary Literature |date=Spring 2007 |volume=48 |issue=1 |pages=29–60 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4489188 |access-date=1 July 2021 |publisher=University of Wisconsin Press|doi=10.1353/cli.2007.0023 |jstor=4489188 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> ''[[Modern Language Association|PMLA]],''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig |title=The Poetry of Sound |journal=PMLA |date=May 2008 |volume=123 |issue=3 |pages=755–761 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25501896 |access-date=1 July 2021 |publisher=Cambridge University Press|jstor=25501896 }}</ref> and ''[[Contemporary Literature (journal)|Critical Inquiry]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig |title=Poetry in the Age of Consumer-Generated Content |journal=Critical Inquiry |date=Summer 2018 |volume=44 |issue=4 |pages=674–705 |doi=10.1086/698173 |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/698173 |access-date=1 July 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Eclipse ==

Dworkin is the founding senior editor of Eclipse, an online archive focusing on digital facsimiles of radical small-press writing from the last quarter of the 20th century.<ref name="Jacket2 Eclipse Interview" /> Dworkin started the archive in 2002 to provide readers and scholars with access to avant-garde works that were no longer available in print from their original publishers; Eclipse later expanded to publish selected new works and born-digital publications in the spirit of those earlier presses.<ref name="2017 Entropy">{{cite web |last1=Higgs |first1=Christopher |title=Helping to Redraw the Map of 20th Century Literature: In Conversation with Craig Dworkin, editor of Eclipse online archive of avant-garde writing |url=https://entropymag.org/helping-to-redraw-the-map-of-20th-century-literature-in-conversation-with-craig-dworkin-editor-of-eclipse-online-archive-of-avant-garde-writing/ |website=Entropy Mag |access-date=27 March 2024 |date=1 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170301191214/https://entropymag.org/helping-to-redraw-the-map-of-20th-century-literature-in-conversation-with-craig-dworkin-editor-of-eclipse-online-archive-of-avant-garde-writing/ |archive-date=2017-03-01 }}</ref> The archive's name is an homage to [[Douglas Messerli]]’s Sun & Moon press.<ref name="2017 Entropy" />

Eclipse includes high-resolution scans of every page of its included texts, most from Dworkin's personal collection,<ref name="Jacket2 Eclipse Interview" /> in an attempt to "conserve ... the facture and material specificity of the book or printed document as an object."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dworkin |first1=Craig |title=Hypermnesia |journal=Boundary 2|date=Fall 2009 |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=77–95 |doi=10.1215/01903659-2009-021 |url=http://eclipsearchive.org/Editor/DworkinHypermnesia.pdf |access-date=27 March 2024 |publisher=Duke University Press}}</ref> Dworkin co-manages the archive with Danny Snelson, assistant professor of English at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Snelson |first1=Danny |title=An Elegy for Jimmy & Lucy's House of "K" (1984–1989) |url=https://post45.org/2023/06/an-elegy-for-ijimmy-and-lucys-house-of-k-1984-1989/#footnote_8_20645 |website=Post45 |access-date=27 March 2024 |date=6 June 2023}}</ref>
